avatar_choice: Already selected by the user in Google Vids

scenes.title: The hook
scenes.line: A support bot should know when it has an answer, and when it needs to ask.
scenes.short: A useful support bot knows when to answer, and when to ask.
scenes.lens: 50 mm full-frame equivalent, f/2.8 intent; chest-up medium shot, eye-level camera.
scenes.move: One almost imperceptible straight push-in, no more than three percent over eight seconds; no lateral movement.
scenes.action: Begin with relaxed shoulders and an attentive expression; make one small open-palm gesture, then settle.

scenes.title: What this project is
scenes.line: This project brings policy answers, document checks, conversation context, and support tickets into one service desk.
scenes.short: Policy answers, document checks, context, and tickets come together in one service desk.
scenes.lens: 35 mm full-frame equivalent, f/4 intent; waist-up medium shot at the same eye level and axis.
scenes.move: Locked tripod; no zoom, pan, tilt or focus change.
scenes.action: Stay comfortably centered; use a small inclusive hand gesture on the list, without counting on fingers.

scenes.title: The real service desk
scenes.line: Here’s the actual interface: ask a question, share a document, or pick up an existing support ticket.
scenes.source: Run the actual FastAPI application and record its customer page at localhost:8000. Use synthetic data and a masked customer role key.
scenes.frame: Full-screen browser capture at 1920×1080, with text large enough to read. Start on the page title and chat/upload panels; use one slow downward scroll to reveal the tickets panel.
scenes.motion: Hold the top for two seconds, scroll smoothly during seconds two to five, then hold. No orbit, simulated handheld motion or perspective warp.
scenes.label: Actual local UI · synthetic data

scenes.title: Policy evidence
scenes.line: Before searching policies, it checks access, dates, and versions. Then the answer has to cite its evidence.
scenes.short: Access, dates, and versions come first. Then the answer must cite its evidence.
scenes.lens: 50 mm full-frame equivalent, f/2.8 intent; chest-up medium shot, eye-level.
scenes.move: Locked tripod; match scene 01's camera axis.
scenes.action: A small nod on the first sentence; keep the second sentence clear and matter-of-fact.

scenes.title: A cited fixture answer
scenes.line: Here’s an offline demo answer. Its citation shows the document, version, and section behind the response.
scenes.source: Run python scripts/demo_t4.py and record the real first supported answer and its citation. This uses FakeClock/FakeLLM; keep that fact visible.
scenes.frame: Terminal capture with a neutral dark theme and at least 24-pixel text. Crop to the query, Answer and Citations rows from the actual output.
scenes.motion: Static for five seconds, then a small editor crop toward the citation, maximum 110 percent. Do not retype or replace the answer.
scenes.label: Offline fixture demo · FakeClock / FakeLLM

scenes.title: Refusing without evidence
scenes.line: And when there’s no supporting policy, this fixture run refuses instead of filling the gap with a guess.
scenes.source: In the real scripts/demo_t4.py output, record the no-evidence scenario and its actual refusal status.
scenes.frame: Same terminal theme and font as scene 05. Show the question, refusal answer and empty citations together.
scenes.motion: Locked crop; one editor-added underline or outline can draw attention to Refusal=True. Preserve the original text.
scenes.label: Offline fixture demo · no supporting evidence

scenes.title: The retrieval path
scenes.line: Those filters happen before scoring. Restricted or inactive documents aren’t supposed to become evidence for the current question.
scenes.source: Record the rendered architecture diagram in the actual README, or the corresponding filter code with identifiers visible. This is an architecture explanation, not a live request trace.
scenes.frame: Show authorization, applicable dates, latest version and hybrid retrieval in one readable crop.
scenes.motion: One slow editor crop from the filter node toward retrieval, 100 to 108 percent. Keep edges straight.
scenes.label: Architecture · filtering before similarity

scenes.title: Controlled updates
scenes.line: Updating the bot’s knowledge has a checklist too: validate it, check quality, approve it, then wait.
scenes.short: New knowledge passes validation, quality checks, approval, and a maintenance window.
scenes.lens: 35 mm full-frame equivalent, f/4 intent; waist-up medium shot, same eye level.
scenes.action: Rest one hand lightly near the desk; deliver the list naturally, without a formal presentation pose.

scenes.title: Maintenance activation
scenes.line: In this simulated day, activation waits outside the window, then proceeds after approval when the configured window opens.
scenes.source: Run python scripts/demo_t1.py. Record actual lines showing activation blocked at 01:30 and approved activation at 02:00, if the current real output contains them.
scenes.frame: Readable terminal crop containing both lines and the script's offline FakeClock/FakeLLM identification.
scenes.motion: Hold the blocked line for three seconds; use a single editor emphasis on the activated line for the rest. No altered timestamps.
scenes.label: Offline maintenance simulation · FakeClock / FakeLLM

scenes.title: Health rollback
scenes.line: A scripted health failure follows, and the active snapshot rolls back. That behavior uses a fake clock.
scenes.source: Record the actual health-failure and auto-rollback lines from scripts/demo_t1.py. Do not claim a real provider outage was induced.
scenes.frame: Same terminal appearance as scene 09, with the previous and restored ACTIVE version readable.
scenes.motion: Static; highlight the restored version using a simple editor outline. Keep the frame steady.
scenes.label: Offline simulation · scripted health failure

scenes.title: From upload to fields
scenes.line: Documents follow a different path: validate the upload, extract visible fields, and compare them with the customer’s message.
scenes.short: Validate the upload, extract visible fields, then compare them with the customer's message.
scenes.lens: 50 mm full-frame equivalent, f/2.8 intent; chest-up medium shot, same eye level.
scenes.move: Gentle straight push-in, no more than two percent over the whole shot.
scenes.action: Brief glance toward the lower desk area, then maintain eye contact; one small explanatory gesture.

scenes.title: Actual invoice extraction
scenes.line: Here, the clean invoice fixture exposes its order, date, and amount. Missing fields should stay empty, never invented.
scenes.source: Upload tests/fixtures/task2/clean.png through the real UI. For the customer message, use the order/date/amount actually visible in that fixture. Record actual extraction results.
scenes.frame: Show the upload filename and returned fields; use a tight crop of the document panel, with text remaining readable.
scenes.motion: Hold the input for two seconds and the actual extraction result for six; trim a long processing wait with a clearly ordinary cut.
scenes.label: Actual OCR · synthetic invoice fixture

scenes.title: Conflicting information
scenes.line: If the message and invoice disagree, the next step is clarification, with conflicting values shown to the customer.
scenes.source: Submit the mismatched invoice fixture with a deliberately conflicting synthetic customer message. Record the actual response; retain the original file and message for verification.
scenes.frame: Same upload-panel crop as scene 12, showing the compared values and clarification text.
scenes.motion: Static result crop with an editor outline around the conflicting pair. Do not generate replacement field values.
scenes.label: Actual upload check · conflicting synthetic values

scenes.title: Language and context
scenes.line: Conversations can switch language, keep recent context, and protect recognized names and order details while responses are translated.
scenes.short: Conversations keep context across language changes, while recognized names and order details stay protected.
scenes.lens: 50 mm full-frame equivalent, f/2.8 intent; chest-up medium shot.
scenes.move: Locked tripod. Match the approved reference framing precisely.
scenes.action: Use an easy conversational tone and a slight pause after language; keep gestures restrained.

scenes.title: Corrections win
scenes.line: This test checks an order correction: keep the latest value, and mark the older one as superseded.
scenes.source: Run python -m pytest -v tests/test_task6.py::test_correction_overrides_earlier_value. Record the actual test name and outcome. Show its source assertions if extra context is needed.
scenes.frame: Terminal and, optionally, a side-by-side crop of the actual test source. Use readable type, not a generated chat reenactment.
scenes.motion: One cut from the selected test name to its real result. Keep eight seconds total.
scenes.label: Offline automated test · correction handling

scenes.title: Entity bytes and isolation
scenes.line: Other tests check order details stay intact, and different customers keep separate conversations, even with simultaneous requests.
scenes.source: Run python -m pytest -v tests/test_task6.py::test_entities_preserved_across_languages tests/test_task6.py::test_concurrent_sessions_isolated. Record the real named results.
scenes.frame: Show both exact test names and their terminal outcomes at readable scale.
scenes.motion: Static capture; no scroll while the names are being read. An editor outline can move once between the two rows.
scenes.label: Offline tests · entity bytes / concurrent isolation

scenes.title: Risk is separate
scenes.line: A calm message can still describe a serious problem. High-risk detection stays separate from the sentiment classifier’s prediction.
scenes.short: Calm wording can describe serious trouble. Risk detection stays separate from sentiment.
scenes.lens: 50 mm full-frame equivalent, f/2.8 intent; chest-up medium shot.
scenes.move: A restrained straight push-in of two percent, with no angle change.
scenes.action: Become attentive without looking alarmed; keep the sentence calm and direct, with no dramatic expression.

scenes.title: Calm high-risk scenarios
scenes.line: Calm compromise, duplicate-payment, and legal-threat scenarios have named tests. The escalation decision does not depend on provider sentiment.
scenes.source: Run python -m pytest -v tests/test_task5.py::test_calm_account_compromise_escalates tests/test_task5.py::test_calm_duplicate_payment_escalates tests/test_task5.py::test_calm_legal_threat_escalates tests/test_assisted_sentiment.py::test_high_risk_independent_of_provider_positive_label. Record the actual named outcomes.
scenes.frame: Record the exact named results; keep high-risk vocabulary and PASS status readable. This is offline contract verification.
scenes.motion: Static terminal crop with a single gentle crop shift if needed; no generated alert animation.
scenes.label: Offline tests · separate rule-based high-risk detector

scenes.title: A complete handoff
scenes.line: When support needs a ticket, missing details stay as questions. The system shouldn’t invent a customer or order.
scenes.short: Missing ticket details stay as questions; the system should not invent them.
scenes.lens: 35 mm full-frame equivalent, f/4 intent; waist-up medium shot.
scenes.move: Locked tripod, on the same side of the axis as earlier wide shots.
scenes.action: Open one palm briefly on questions, then return to a relaxed neutral pose.

scenes.title: Ticket draft
scenes.line: The draft asks for mandatory information first. Supplied details move into the final structured ticket and its handoff.
scenes.source: In the real customer UI, ask for a ticket without supplying all mandatory fields. Record the actual questions and draft; enter synthetic details only.
scenes.frame: A readable crop of Your tickets and its missing-field questions. Keep any access key masked or outside the capture.
scenes.motion: Hold the missing-field message, then show the completed synthetic form with a hard cut. No fake success overlay.
scenes.label: Actual local UI · synthetic ticket draft

scenes.title: Queue and routing
scenes.line: With no eligible agent configured, the ticket queues. Routing and service deadlines use configured skills and business hours.
scenes.source: Submit the completed synthetic ticket in the real UI and record the actual QUEUED state. Use scripts/demo_t3.py for a separately labelled offline SLA explanation if desired.
scenes.frame: Ticket ID, issue and actual status in one clear crop. No external email or paging UI.
scenes.motion: Static hold. Add one small editor label for local queue, without altering the actual result.
scenes.label: Actual local queue · external delivery not configured

scenes.title: Evidence before claims
scenes.line: Tests check how the system behaves. Model quality is a separate question, especially when quotas interrupt evaluation.
scenes.short: Passing tests do not make a quota-limited model evaluation valid.
scenes.lens: 50 mm full-frame equivalent, f/2.8 intent; chest-up medium shot.
scenes.move: Locked camera; no dramatic push or rack focus.
scenes.action: Direct, candid delivery; a small pause between sentences, with a neutral expression.

scenes.title: Results and limitations
scenes.line: The report keeps the invalid policy run, the fallback score, and translation failures visible, alongside actual test evidence.
scenes.source: Record the current REPORT measured-results table and the actual successful CI workflow. Show T4 12/20 plus INVALID and 10/72 provider failures, T5 fallback 20/48, and translation HTTP 429.
scenes.frame: Use two four-second evidence crops: report status, then actual CI/test evidence. Add an editor label with the recorded source commit and date.
scenes.motion: Two hard cuts only; no rapid scrolling or tiny full-page capture. Keep the invalid-run label beside the 12/20 count.
scenes.label: Measured evidence · invalid run / fallback / quota limits

scenes.title: Close with the repository
scenes.line: The code, setup steps, and evidence are in the repository. It’s a local demo, with its limits documented.
scenes.short: Explore the code and evidence in the repository. Current status: local demo.
scenes.lens: 50 mm full-frame equivalent, f/2.8 intent; chest-up medium shot.
scenes.move: Locked camera; hold a stable composition for the closing card.
scenes.action: Small relaxed smile after speaking; keep the pose steady for the final editor-added repository card.
